title: Practical proof protocol - runtime candidate notes
text:
Context:
- Candidate: applied for Senior Runtime Engineer (inference runtime). Interview loop completed 2025-08-28. I ran the take-home and did a follow-up pairing session (30m) 2025-08-29.
- Purpose: capture contradictions between verbal claims, take-home results, and live pairing. Propose a short practical confirmation protocol to reduce hiring risk before offering.

Quick summary (one-paragraph):
Candidate presents as very experienced with attention and KV cache behaviour; strong systems instincts; claims deep familiarity with batching heuristics and kernel tuning. Take-home produced a workable gRPC batching shim but performance numbers are lower than claimed (50-60% of expected throughput vs their stated past projects). Pairing revealed comfort with debugging but unfamiliarity with our specific quantized inference flow (we saw confusion around cache invalidation on model-side partial queries). This doc lists hypotheses for the mismatch, concrete micro-tests to validate critical skills, rubric for pass/fail, and recommended next steps.

Observed contradictions and hypotheses:
1) Throughput claim vs take-home numbers:
   - Claim: "I optimized inference throughput by 2-3x at my last role via batching policy and kernel choices."
   - Evidence: take-home batching shim works functionally, but steady-state token/sec is ~55% of the candidate's stated baseline.
   - Hypotheses: A) candidate overstated prior context (worked on orchestration, not kernel-level tuning), B) candidate's optimizations rely on hardware we don't have (A100 v.s. T4), C) implementation details (KV cache warmup, micro-batching) not properly simulated in take-home.

2) KV cache / prefix handling confusion:
   - Claim: "I always use prefix-aware caching and single-pass KV reuse."
   - Evidence: during pairing they suggested invalidating cache on any partial session change; that leads to throughput regressions and is inconsistent with our inference flow.
   - Hypotheses: A) candidate has conceptual knowledge but not production exposure to LLM prefix caching patterns; B) different product constraints at prior role forced simpler invalidation rules.

3) Quantization and numeric stability:
   - Claim: comfort shipping INT8/4-bit quantized models with negligible regression.
   - Evidence: gave a generic description of symmetric quantization but could not articulate fallback strategies for hallucination/precision loss or explain per-layer sensitivity analysis.
   - Hypotheses: candidate has theoretical familiarity but not hands-on experience with post-quantization calibration workflows.

Risk implications (if hired without additional validation):
- Medium: Wrong assumptions about KV caching could cause regressive design choices on our serving paths that increase latency for multi-turn sessions.
- Medium-high: Overconfidence on quantization could lead to poor model regressions if candidate responsible for rollout/quality checks.
- Low-medium: Implementation pace risk if candidate needs ramp to our infra (different kernel stack and perf tooling).

Practical proof protocol (3 focused micro-tests; each scoped to 2-4 hours):
A) Batching & steady-state throughput microtest (2-4h)
   - Goal: confirm candidate can produce an end-to-end micro-benchmark matching our runtime constraints.
   - Deliverable: local script + README that runs 1) an in-process batching shim feeding a small LLM (fp16 or 4-bit simulated), 2) a load generator that ramps to steady-state, and 3) a report with token/sec and p50/p95 latencies and explanation of tuning knobs used.
   - Success criteria (pass): candidate demonstrates >80% of the throughput improvement they claim relative to a clear baseline and documents where hardware differences matter.

B) KV cache behavior case study (2-3h)
   - Goal: practical understanding of prefix reuse, invalidation edge-cases, and correctness/perf tradeoffs.
   - Deliverable: short doc + a small test harness that simulates multi-turn queries with prefix edits; demonstrates at least two cache strategies (aggressive invalidate vs. prefix-preserving) and shows perf/correctness tradeoff.
   - Success criteria: candidate explains point-of-failure scenarios, provides metrics showing latency win for prefix-preserving in typical RLHF-like multi-turn workload, and notes fallback policy for rare invalidation cases.

C) Quantization regression triage (2-4h)
   - Goal: confirm ability to spot per-layer sensitivity and propose a safe rollout plan.
   - Deliverable: candidate runs a quick calibration on a provided 2M-token prompt set (we supply lightweight hooks) and shows an analysis: per-layer sensitivity plot (even rough), mitigation plan (mixed precision or selective float fallback), and a short A/B evaluation plan.
   - Success criteria: candidate finds at least one per-layer hotspot, proposes a clear mitigation approach, and outlines how to tie quality checks to our eval pipeline.

Evaluation rubric (simple pass/fail for each micro-test + gestalt):
- Clear deliverable produced on time: +1
- Demonstrated reasoning about tradeoffs (not just code): +1
- Metrics match claimed improvements (within stated hardware caveats): +1
- Quality of write-up (can a peer reproduce in <1h): +1
- Fail thresholds: <2/4 across deliverables or major conceptual error on KV cache/quantization => escalate as fail.

Interview notes (raw snippets):
- "I usually let the runtime batcher pick micro-batch sizes based on percentiles" -> asked how their percentiles are estimated; answer: "histogram from traces, prune outliers" (no mention of continuous decaying window).
- When asked about a scenario where prefix tokens are edited mid-session they said "evict everything" and later backtracked to "we could try partial recompute but it's complicated".
- Comfortable writing C++ perf hooks but prefers Python for orchestration/prototyping.
- Strong system-level intuition: excellent hypotheticals about cross-GPU KV sharding but little evidence they implemented the shard placement logic in prod.

Recommended next steps (tactical):
1) Offer the practical proof protocol as a paid short contracting exercise (4-8 hours total with a small stipend). This reduces false positive risk and checks critical areas.
2) Share micro-test A and B first; if candidate passes both, proceed with C.
3) If candidate fails A or B, stop and capture failure modes; consider candidate for an IC2/IC3 role depending on gaps rather than Senior.

Notes to hiring committee / DM to Ava:
- I'm leaning toward proceeding conditionally (paid microtests) rather than outright offer. Candidate has good instincts but some signal mismatches.
- If we go to microtests, be explicit about hardware caveats (we use A40s in staging; candidate mentioned A100 optimizations).

Unresolved questions for follow-up (quick items):
- Clarify candidate's exact previous infra (what GPUs/kernels they tuned) -> ask HR for project PRs/links.
- Get sample traces from candidate (their prior repo) if available to judge percentiles approach.
- Confirm comfort level with Rust/C++ vs Python for production runtime work.

To-do (my checklist):
- [ ] Draft microtest A instructions and minimal harness by 2025-09-03 (assign to Marcus for infra bits).
- [ ] Confirm stipend amount and legal template with Hiring Ops by 2025-09-04.
- [ ] Send short note to candidate with conditional next steps by 2025-09-05.

Slack/links I referenced in loop: #eng-runtime, DM to @ava, ticket JIRA-ENG-3421 (microtests).

Raw gut verdict (private):
- 60/100. Smart, practical thinker, but needs verification on production perf/quantization chops. Paid microtests should resolve majority of uncertainty.

End of note.
